verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that a skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` that must include `name` and `description`, explain where Codex discovers skills (`.agents/skills`), and describe a guided skill creator that asks what the skill does and when it should trigger. Community use of the skill-creator and a hands-on probe showing a `SKILL.md` with valid name frontmatter corroborate this. Missing for 10: a verbatim copy-paste SKILL.md template with an explicit YAML frontmatter example in the docs, and documentation of optional frontmatter fields beyond name and description.

support.subject: As a developer, I can author a new skill from a documented template — a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter — without reverse-engineering existing skills

citations.quote: A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file plus optional scripts and references. The `SKILL.md` file must include `name` and `description`.
The creator asks what the skill does, when it should trigger, and whether it should stay instruction-only or include scripts.
Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.
The skills that matter most to this user are ones they build themselves with the skill-creator skill for proprietary workflows
